problem: Prior MLLM-driven robot navigation typically re-explores environments each time and does not reuse previously traversed paths, which wastes effort and hurts efficiency. The abstract gives no more detail on specific baselines.
motivation: Reusing memory of previously traversed paths can reduce re-exploration and improve navigation efficiency and path retracing for terrestrial robots. A hybrid architecture is used so that the MLLM handles high-level decisions while a reactive controller handles low-level alignment.
key_idea: A customized MLLM interprets camera images and issues navigation commands, and a memory of previously traversed paths lets a Unitree GO1 retrace routes rather than re-explore, through a hybrid deliberation and reactive controller.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation details can be cited. The abstract claims that memory-driven navigation improves path retracing and overall performance in a hallway-like environment, and that separating deliberation from reactive alignment is a useful design.
method: Customized MLLM: interprets camera images and generates navigation commands.
Memory-based navigation: stores previously traversed paths and reuses them to reduce re-exploration.
Hybrid controller, deliberation unit: produces high-level commands.
Hybrid controller, reactive controller: handles robot alignment at low level.
Platform: Unitree GO1 quadruped with an onboard camera capturing environment images.

setting.training_data: not stated in abstract (customized/fine-tuned MLLM implied)
setting.action_space: high-level navigation commands from the MLLM plus reactive alignment control (details not given)

results: The abstract states qualitatively that experiments in a hallway-like environment show memory-driven navigation improves path retracing and overall performance. No quantitative results or baselines are given.
limitations: Evaluated only in a hallway-like environment, so generalization is unclear.
